preconditions.description: Contract must be activated (trading open, fees enabled, swap enabled, token hold enabled, auto claim enabled, reward as tokens enabled)
Attacker must hold at least minRewardBalance (50000 * 10^9 tokens) to be included in rewards
Contract must have BNB balance for rewards (mainBnbPoolSize is 5000 ether)

violation_target.exploit_hint: Call setClaimRewardAsTokensPercentage(100) as attacker to set your reward claim percentage to 100%. This will cause all your BNB rewards to be converted to LLG tokens instead of receiving BNB. Since the function has no access control, anyone can call it. After setting to 100%, claim rewards to receive LLG tokens instead of BNB. This bypasses the intended restriction that only the contract owner should be able to configure this setting.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in the LLG contract's setClaimRewardAsTokensPercentage function. This function lacks any access control modifier (like onlyOwner) and allows any caller to set their own percentage. The function only validates that percentage <= 100, then sets _claimRewardAsTokensPercentage[msg.sender] = percentage. This means an attacker can set their percentage to 100%, causing all their future BNB rewards to be converted to LLG tokens instead. This bypasses the intended restriction that only the contract owner should be able to configure this setting.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Ensure the contract is activated (trading open, fees enabled, etc.) by impersonating the owner. 2. Give the attacker enough LLG tokens to meet the minRewardBalance requirement (50,000 * 10^9 tokens). 3. Fund the contract with BNB for rewards (mainBnbPoolSize is 5000 ether). 4. Call setClaimRewardAsTokensPercentage(100) as the attacker. 5. Trigger a reward claim to verify the percentage is set to 100%. 6. The oracle will check that LLG.claimRewardAsTokensPercentage(attacker_address) == 100.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Impersonate the contract owner to activate the contract and set up necessary configurations. 2. Use deal() to give the attacker enough LLG tokens (at least 50,000 * 10^9). 3. Use deal() to fund the contract with BNB for rewards (at least 5000 ether). 4. As the attacker, call setClaimRewardAsTokensPercentage(100). 5. Verify the percentage was set correctly. 6. Optionally trigger a reward claim to demonstrate the effect.
